title: Release TaskFlow
goal: Package the API, verify it in CI, deploy API + web, and prove the production release with smoke tests and rollback notes.
steps: Write a simple Dockerfile, build it, then improve caching and runtime size.
Run API + PostgreSQL in Compose and fix the `localhost` networking mistake intentionally.
Create a pull-request CI workflow with checkout, deterministic pnpm install, typecheck, tests, and build.
Set workflow token permissions to the minimum required.
Add concurrency/branch protection so obsolete or failing changes do not release.
Document the production migration step and compatibility requirement.
Deploy the API and verify health/readiness.
Deploy Next.js to Vercel with production API configuration.
Verify production CORS, DNS, and TLS.
Run post-deploy smoke tests and inspect logs/metrics.
Write and rehearse the rollback decision/runbook.
evidence: A clean Git diff or file-tree change
Browser, HTTP, database, test, container, or CI evidence that proves the behavior
One deliberate failure, the evidence you used, and the root-cause fix
A short explanation of why the final responsibility lives in the chosen layer
completion: I can reproduce one key part without the walkthrough.
I can explain one trade-off I deliberately chose.
I can show one failure that my tests, constraints, or runbook now protects against.
